title: Single-seater racing in the browser with tyre wear, DRS and a pit stop you have to make, made with Claude Code
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
This is a short-race open-wheel racer for the browser, on desktop or phone. You start from a 20-car grid with a five-light start on one of three made-up circuits: a coastal track, a northern forest and a desert circuit under lights.

**How Claude was used:** all the game code was written with Claude Code:

* **Driving feel first.** One car, one track, and lots of rounds telling Claude what felt off with steering, braking and grip.
* **Race systems one at a time.** Tyre wear (softs are quick but drop off early), ERS boost on straights, DRS when you’re within a second of the car ahead, and slipstreaming rivals.
* **The mandatory pit stop.** Call it with P or the BOX button, pick tyres on pit entry, and the crew changes all four wheels in under three seconds. Getting the pit lane, the stop and the rejoin working together took the most back and forth.
* **Setup before the race:** start tyres, wing level and brake bias.
* **A broadcast-style HUD last:** a live timing tower with gaps, a steering-wheel dash with shift lights, tyre and energy readouts, and a circuit map.

**Other tools and assets:**

* Car model “F1 2022 {FREE!!}” by 3dblender\_1 on Sketchfab (CC BY 4.0, recoloured)
* Tree models by several Sketchfab creators (CC BY 4.0)
* Pit crew character and animations from Mixamo
* Textures and skies from Poly Haven (CC0)
* Engine, crowd, wheel gun, tyre and crash sounds from Freesound (CC0)

**Cost:** free to play in the browser, no sign-up or download.

[https://vinish.dev/gridburn-racing-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/gridburn-racing-browser-based-game)

Would like feedback on the tyre wear. Does the soft-tyre drop-off feel right over a short race?
